one_month_reasoning: Window Oct 2-31, 2026. Checked the SEC filing index and IREN's news page on Oct 2: no 8-K since the Aug 27 FY26 results, no Horizon 2 acceptance and no Q1 FY27 results date yet. Last year's Q1 came out Nov 6, 2025, so the print most likely lands Nov 5-6, outside the window; the AGM is Nov 24. In-window possibilities are unscheduled: Horizon 2-4 acceptance by Microsoft (targeted Q4 CY26, grace to early Q2 2027), contract signings for the +0.5GW 2027 build, GPU financings, ATM issuance, and the Oct 27-28 FOMC with the 10y at 5.24%. These roughly cancel, so I keep round 1's lognormal: centred about $40.5, monthly sigma about 0.29 (107% annual vol / 3.5, trimmed slightly), essentially symmetric. Unchanged from rounds 1-3: neither the GPU-life work nor the round-4 site and discount-rate fixes touch anything scheduled before Oct 31.

fair_value.method: 0.4 x split-rate central DCF $7.7 + 0.6 x EV/EBITDA $40.2 at Oct-27 = $27.2 (with the limited-liability DCF expectation $13.7: $29.6; with the single-rate central DCF $6.5: $26.7). DCF values each inventory site once with contracted cash flows at 7.0-10.0% and everything else at 11.5%; EV/EBITDA is 7.5x $6.0bn NTM EBITDA less $21.9bn net debt over 575m shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site cohort FCFF, split-rate central at Oct-27 $7.7 (single-rate 11.5% $6.5; expectation $13.7 split / $12.9 single). Contracted ARR $4.68bn (Microsoft $1.94bn, 2026 non-IG $2.06bn, NVIDIA $0.68bn) at contract terms; S04/S05/S09/S10 probability-weighted at $20m/MW; 2028+ pipeline option ~0, floored at rights cost; refresh $32m/MW at 6 yrs; FY27 capex $25bn; net debt $0.6bn; 455m shares

inputs_detail.value: Site-by-site: every inventory site (S01-S17) appears once. Signed contracts at contract terms and timing; under-construction uncontracted sites probability-weighted (success vs 1.5-yr delay at 0.9x price) with their data-center capex in both branches; 2028+ pipeline as an option (built only if NPV>0) with a floor at what IREN paid for comparable power rights
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 used a generic capacity path to 1,925MW IT that double-counted Sweetwater 1 phase 1 (F05), pooled 2026 contracted capacity at $15.7m/MW (F06) and put the NVIDIA contract on ~30MW (F03). The inventory's coverage matrix and flags drive the rebuild; FY27-FY45 explicit, then a steady-state refresh terminal per slot.

inputs_detail.value: 200MW IT at $9.7m/MW-yr ($1.94bn/yr) for 5 yrs per tranche: H1 50MW from Aug-26, H2-4 150MW from mid-Jan-27 (Q4-26 target, grace to Q2-27); remaining capex ~$5.9bn in FY27 (75% of $5.81bn GPUs + ~$1.5bn data center)
inputs_detail.derivation: TCV $9.7bn, 5-yr average term, four tranches, H1 accepted Aug-2026 (8-K). Remaining-capex split is my judgment (H1 is one quarter of the GPUs; data center $14-16m/MW). Direction of rights: Microsoft prepaid 20% of TCV ($1.94bn) and IREN credits it back against fees in years 3-5 of each tranche, so the model adds the ~$0.93bn still receivable in FY27 and deducts $1.94bn of credits over years 3-5; IREN Limited guarantees the SPV debt allocated to a tranche Microsoft terminates (contingent, not valued; termination unlikely).

inputs_detail.value: $2.06bn ARR (= >$4bn 2026 ARR less Microsoft): Prince George $0.50bn on ~28MW IT (air-cooled 2.25-yr terms + liquid from Dec-26), Mackenzie $1.25bn on ~58MW IT and Childress air-cooled $0.31bn on ~14MW IT, both $21.7m/MW for 3 yrs from Nov/Dec-26; capex Mackenzie $2.9bn, Childress $0.8bn, Prince George liquid $0.35bn
inputs_detail.derivation: Fixes F06. ARR by site: Prince George $0.5bn (Q3 FY26 footnote, the latest of three conflicting figures); Mackenzie and Childress split by GPU count (~40k of the 50k B300 to Mackenzie). 300MW IT total for 2026 (200 Microsoft + 100 other). Terms: portfolio ~4-yr weighted term including Microsoft/NVIDIA implies ~2.7 yrs for these; Mackenzie GPU capex $2.7-2.8bn implied by the $2.4bn 90% financing. These contracts only just recover GPU capex within the term (revenue ~2.3x annual, ~2.2-yr payback), so the tail carries much of their value.

inputs_detail.value: 60MW gross = ~43MW IT, $0.68bn ARR ($15.8m/IT MW) for 5 yrs from ~Apr-27; Dell hardware $1.6bn + $0.1bn retrofit
inputs_detail.derivation: Fixes F03 (round 3 used ~30MW). IT vs gross is not disclosed; I treat 60 as gross at 0.714 IT/gross, the ratio that reconciles IREN's 1,210MW gross with 0.8GW IT for 2027 (280MW gross of air-cooled retrofits giving 200MW IT). ARR is outside the >$4bn 2026 figure (Dell 8-K $3.7bn -> $4.4bn). NVIDIA's right to buy up to 30m IREN shares at $70 runs against IREN holders: ~7.5m expected to vest at a 150k-GPU fleet, valued ~$0.07bn and deducted.

inputs_detail.value: S04 Childress air 136MW IT from ~Aug-27, p=0.85; S05 Horizons 5-6 100MW IT from ~Dec-27, p=0.75; S09 Canal Flats 21MW IT from ~Nov-27, p=0.75; S10 Sweetwater 1 phase 1 200MW IT from ~Jan-28, p=0.70. On contract: $20m/MW, 3 yrs; failure branch: 1.5 yrs later at $18m. GPUs $35m/MW and data center (S05/S10 $19.8m/MW; retrofits ~$3m/MW), both +10% for the CFO's per-MW cost inflation
inputs_detail.derivation: Probabilities: S04 retrofits existing powered halls at a site whose 2026 capacity sold out and management cites late-stage talks at ~$25m/MW (company claim, unverified); S05/S09 lack a customer and S05's GPUs are not ordered; S10 also depends on ERCOT Batch Zero (conditional Base Load; final allocations spring 2027). $20m is the low end of the '>$20m' 3-yr contracts. Data-center capex is spent in both branches, GPUs only once contracted.

inputs_detail.value: Option value: build only if NPV>0. A new liquid-cooled MW at $50m all-in, $20m/MW 3-yr contract then the decay path, has NPV of -$18m/MW at 11.5% (-$9m even at $24m/MW), so the option is worth ~0 at every price in my grid; values are floors: Kiowa $112m (IREN's cost), Nostrum $148m pro rata to MW (10-K price), other powered sites $0.07m/MW gross (Kiowa's cost rate). P(build on schedule): SW1 rest 0.6, SW2 0.5, Kiowa 0.4, Bundey 0.35, Badajoz 0.45, other Spain 0.3
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor: growth earning below WACC should not be in the central case. Valued as round 3's generic growth (no option), the pipeline is worth about -$52 per share, which is why round 3's central case was negative. Probabilities reflect power status (SW1 substation energized; SW2 substation under construction; Kiowa grid studies done; Bundey connection agreement subject to approvals; Spain in permitting) and funding: 2.9GW at $50m/MW is ~$150bn. S17 (unannounced) excluded: no MW disclosed.

inputs_detail.derivation: Mining ends Dec-2026; its ~380MW is the same power as S02-S04 and S07-S09, so it is not added again.

inputs_detail.value: $25bn (site build-up $23.7bn if every under-construction site is contracted; $22.2bn probability-weighted) + $1.3bn unallocated charged at WACC to reach the guide's low end
inputs_detail.derivation: CFO guide $25-30bn (excludes GPUs for new liquid-cooled halls, which fall in FY28). The rest of the guide most likely funds the 2027 liquid-cooled headroom deployments in BC (F09; MW undisclosed, not valued) and early works. Round 3 used the $27.5bn midpoint.

The $1.013bn Microsoft prepayment in deferred revenue (F11) is now modelled explicitly as credits in years 3-5, so it is not also counted as debt.

inputs_detail.value: Single: 11.5% WACC (11/12% 50/50). Split: Microsoft-contract cash flows 7.0%, NVIDIA 7.5%, non-IG developer contracts 10.0% (ARR-weighted 8.4%); everything post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline and terminal at 11.5%
inputs_detail.derivation: Microsoft: secured A-rated debt against this contract at 6.00% blended (SOFR+2.13-2.25%); an unlevered rate of ~65% debt at 6.0% after tax plus ~35% equity at ~11% is 6.8%; +0.2pp for H2-4 completion and managed-services risk gives 7.0%. NVIDIA (S&P AA): no financing closed yet, so +0.5pp over Microsoft. Non-IG AI developers: 9.0% fixed 30-month secured paper at 90% of GPU cost (Mackenzie), plus 45-55% prepayments; ~60% at 9% after tax plus 40% at my 15.2% cost of equity gives ~10%. Equity value is rolled to Oct-27 stream by stream at each stream's rate, net debt at 4.9%.

inputs_detail.value: Central (M0 $20m, re-contract 0.70, 6-yr) per share at Oct-27: single rate $6.5, split rate $7.7 (5-yr $9.2, 7-yr $7.4). Limited-liability expectation over the round-3 grid: single $12.9, split $13.7. Without pipeline floors: split $6.6
inputs_detail.derivation: Bridge from round 3 central -$9.8: removing the generic growth path beyond 0.8GW takes it to about +$4 (round-3 model, no growth); disclosed contract terms by site, the 43MW NVIDIA footprint, cheap retrofits of existing halls and the explicit Microsoft prepayment add about +$5, and the $25bn capex anchor (FY27 capex $27.5bn -> $25bn, but with $1.3bn unallocated) and pipeline floors net to about -$2.5; split rates add +$1.2. The split matters little because during contract terms the contracted cash flows are largely offset by up-front GPU capex discounted at the same low rate; the value sits in the post-contract tail. Sensitivities (split): re-contract 0.55 -$2.2, 0.85 $17.6; M0 $18 -$5.6, $22 $21.0, $24 $34.3; WACC 11% $10.5 / 12% $5.1; contracted rates -/+1pp $7.9 / $7.4; steeper decay $2.8.

inputs_detail.derivation: Site model gives 0.75 x FY28 $5.95bn + 0.25 x FY29 $7.94bn = $6.44bn (probability-weighted; FY28 revenue $8.8bn vs $7.3-7.6bn consensus). Cut ~7% for ramp slippage toward the consensus-anchored $5.8bn of round 3. Higher than round 3 because 2026 contracted capacity now earns its disclosed ~$21.7m/MW rather than $15.7m.
Unchanged (CoreWeave ~7.5x 2027e). The Kerrisdale margin argument I cited in round 3 could not be verified (fact-check), so I rely only on the CoreWeave reference.

bear.story: Horizons 2-4 slip toward the Q2-2027 grace limit, S04/S05/Sweetwater 1 are contracted late or below $20m/MW, and the FY27 build needs heavy ATM issuance and 9%-type GPU debt. Investors price the 2029-30 re-contracting cliff (re-contract ~0.55, where my DCF is about -$2): ~6x depressed NTM EBITDA on ~$23bn of net debt and 600m+ shares.

base.story: $4.7bn of contracted ARR (Microsoft, 2026 developers, NVIDIA) live by mid-2027, the 2027 retrofits contracted near $20m/MW, 0.8GW by early 2028. ~7-7.5x NTM EBITDA of ~$6bn less ~$22bn of net debt over ~575m shares gives $33-40, discounted for funding and re-contract worries that keep the DCF in single digits.

bull.story: 2027 capacity contracted at the ~$25m/MW management cites, NVIDIA financing closes investment-grade, Sweetwater 1 contracted and ERCOT allocations confirmed, and continued evidence that aged GPUs re-contract near original prices (re-contract 0.95: DCF ~$24). Re-rating toward 10x FY29 EBITDA of ~$8-9bn, with pipeline sites starting to look financeable.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at $21. Below it (about 27% under the $28.93 52-week low) the diluted market cap is ~$9.5bn and EV is ~2.2x the $4.68bn of contracted ARR the site inventory confirms (Microsoft, 2026 developers, NVIDIA), near IREN's own bear multiple. The site and discount-rate work leaves the break signals where they were: failed or distressed FY27 funding, a Microsoft Horizon miss beyond the Q2-2027 grace period, a non-IG customer default (they pay the 2026 contracts that the 9% Mackenzie paper is secured on), or hard evidence that aged GPUs re-contract well below ~55% of original prices. My fair value rose to $27, so $21 is not just agreement with my valuation.

reasoning: Round 4. Two fixes. (1) Site coverage: I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the checked inventory so each of the 17 rows appears once. Signed contracts are at their terms and timing: Microsoft 200MW IT at $9.7m for 5 yrs per tranche, with the 20% prepayment modelled in both directions (Microsoft pays up front; IREN credits it back in years 3-5); the 2026 developer contracts at their disclosed $2.06bn ARR (Prince George $0.5bn, Mackenzie and Childress at ~$21.7m/MW, fixing F06's $15.7m pooling); NVIDIA on 60MW gross / ~43MW IT, fixing F03's ~30MW. Sweetwater 1 phase 1 is now inside the 0.8GW 2027 target, not on top of it (F05). The four uncontracted 2027 builds are probability-weighted (0.70-0.85), with data-center capex paid in both branches. The 2028+ pipeline is an option: a new $50m/MW liquid-cooled build at $20m/MW loses ~$18m/MW at 11.5%, so it is worth only the price IREN paid for comparable rights (floors, ~$1 per share). Valued as round 3's generic growth, it would cost ~$52 per share, which is why round 3's central case was negative. Mining residual is counted once, on MW that S02-S09 reuse. FY27 capex is anchored to the guide's low end ($25bn; site build-up $23.7bn). (2) Discount rates: Microsoft-contract cash flows at 7.0%, anchored on the 6.00% A-rated secured financing (re-read the Jun-1 release); NVIDIA 7.5% (AA, no financing yet); unrated developers 10.0%, anchored on the 9% Mackenzie paper; everything else at 11.5%. Central DCF at Oct-27: single $6.5, split $7.7 (round 3 central -$9.8; expectation $16.2 -> $13.7). The split adds only $1.2 because contract-term cash flows are mostly absorbed by up-front GPU capex; the value is in the post-contract tail, which correctly stays at WACC. Per the supervisor, the blend now uses the central DCF: 0.4 x 7.7 + 0.6 x 40.2 = $27.2 (expectation blend $29.6). EV/EBITDA rose from $29.7 to $40.2 because the site fixes raise NTM EBITDA ($5.8bn -> $6.0bn) and remove ~$4.4bn of capex for MW beyond 0.8GW and the guide midpoint from the Oct-27 net debt. GPU life approach and supervisor corrections are kept (life 6 base; 5/7 within $1.5). Ladder: I shift the round-3 ladder up in log space by 34/33 (median $33 -> $34), which is a smaller move than the fair value change ($24.3 -> $27.2), because the gain comes from the EV/EBITDA bridge, where the funding path is the most uncertain input. The DCF still says the fleet barely earns its cost of capital, and spot is $40.65. Scenarios $17 / $35 / $78 at 30/45/25%. Thesis break $21 unchanged. 1-month ladder unchanged. Research this round: two fetches (Jun-1 financing release, Q3 call) to verify the facts I rely on; the inventory was otherwise taken as checked.

In the site model the value-maximising refresh age falls to about 5 (round 3: ~7) because contracted slots carry their actual, higher GPU cost and their below-market contract prices move up to market after the term. I keep 6 as base, which is within $1.5 of 5. Book life is 5 years (10-K, fact-check confirmed; CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5). The re-contract ratio and the new-contract price still drive value; life and the discount-rate split are second order.

discounting.basis: Contracted rate is the ARR-weighted mix of Microsoft 7.0% (anchored on the 6.00% A-rated secured financing against this contract, SOFR+2.13-2.25%, plus completion/operating risk), NVIDIA 7.5% (S&P AA; no financing closed, so +0.5pp) and unrated AI developers 10.0% (anchored on 9.0% fixed 30-month secured paper at 90% of GPU cost plus 45-55% prepayments; between that and WACC). Applied only to cash flows inside each signed contract's term, including that contract's remaining capex and the Microsoft prepayment credits. Post-contract tails, refreshes, uncontracted 2027 builds, pipeline and terminal stay at the 11.5% WACC (cost of equity 15.2%, 11/12% 50/50). Sensitivity: contracted rates -1pp $7.9, +1pp $7.4.
